blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre pesquisas de retórica política a partir de um resumo acadêmico, com densidade técnica e ritmo claro.

body: Esta aula treina **escrever frases claras e corretas (IELTS Writing, TOEFL Writing)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Abstract: “We” and the Politics of Belonging
paras: This study examines the **inclusive pronoun** “we” in a corpus of 400 (fictional) political speeches delivered between 1990 and 2020. **Drawing on** discourse analysis, it **operationalises** inclusion as the proportion of first-person plural pronouns **relative to** first-person singular ones.

**Findings suggest** that speakers **facing** electoral pressure use “we” more frequently, **whereas** incumbents **tend to** favour “I”. **However**, the correlation **weakens markedly** in crisis speeches, **which indicates** that context **mediates** pronoun choice.

**These results should be interpreted with caution**: the corpus is **limited to** English-language texts, and **causal claims** cannot be sustained. **Further research** is needed on **non-electoral** settings.

items.q: The study covers speeches from 1990 to 2020.
The authors claim a causal link.

blocks.body: Resumos usam **voz impessoal**, **hedging** (*suggest, tend to, indicate*) e **nominalizações**. Evite *prove*; prefira *suggest* ou *indicate*.
*Significant* em estatística é termo técnico, não é sinônimo de *importante*.

items.s: ___ on discourse analysis, the study examines speeches. (drawing)
Findings ___ that speakers use “we” more often. (suggest)
Speakers facing pressure use “we”, ___ incumbents favour “I”. (whereas)

items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

prompts.model: The corpus is limited to English.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence abstract about a fictional study on speech length, with method, finding and limitation.
blocks.model: This study examines the length of 200 (fictional) public lectures. Drawing on audience surveys, it relates length to reported attention. Findings suggest that attention declines after twenty minutes, whereas interactive segments sustain it. However, the correlation weakens in expert audiences. The sample is limited to university settings. Further research is needed.
